The moment you boot up Republic Commando is the moment your realize this isn't your usual Star Wars games.

Presented in a darker, militaristic tone, you're placed in the shoes of Boss, a freshly manufactured clone, whose the leader of a commando squad of four. The opening epitomizes the message of the game, that you're a soldier and you have to rely on your squad-mates- as a side-note, look up during the short scene on Kimino, that's the attention to detail this game has. The art-style is harsher and the droids have an threating growl to their voices (fuck those whiny voices Lucas went with). It certainly feels unique since it uses its own soundtrack instead of constantly using John Williams pieces as a crutch. Stylistically, the game is beautiful, with a absolutely rocking soundtrack that knows when to throw in those vocals and drum-beats. Graphically, it's a 2005 game and console port, at 60 fps and proper lighting it's better than the original xbox version for sure. However, I believe it's the art-style instead of the textures that carries the visual direction. 

The actual gameplay harkens back to Rainbow Six with how you use your AI partners to clear levels and focus fire. Some of my favorite aspects of the game are the fact that you can 'prep' for battle. You can order a sniper to sit back or have one of your guys bombard the enemy from grenadier nest. Now you can only do this through context sensitive actions, but it's more a feature of the level design that rewards player thought than a "you can only proceed after using a laser-designated airstrike on these helpless sand people".

The AI is very compentent too. They will require revival, but that's only on the hardest sections of the game. I never felt like they were idiotic, and actually they keep up with you extremely well. It's no F.E.A.R, but for a squad-based shooter, the AI never failed me on the several play-throughs I've had both past and present.

Augmenting this squad is your own weaponry. The standard blaster is honestly a peashooter to me, but you get a motherfucking shotgun in a Star-wars game, and it is god-damn awesome. The standard blaster can be switched to both a sniper rifle and an anti-tank grenade launcher, allowing to have a total of four weapons (one weapon you can pick up from an enemy soldier) with three types of grenades. You also have a blade-fist, and like Halo, your melee attack is brutal and effective in close-combat. In total, you have a solution for every problem and ammo is given often enough to use all your tools while given sparingly enough to not go willy-nilly with sniper and rpg shots.

This game has become one of my favorite Star Wars games mostly because of the characters and story. Your three squad-mates have plenty of memorable quips and though they were stereotypical in their personalities, they give that Star Wars flair that prevents the game from being a super grim-dark slog. I'd never consider them annoying and by the end of the game you really detect how the characters have become more brothers than comrades-at-arms.  Story-wise you get some background information on some of the Clone-war plot-lines from the Prequels. However you never have a moment where it overly masturbates over the prequels' storylines or characters, it plays it straight and the only time you ever see a truly iconic character from Star Wars is once. RC is it's own game and story inside the Star Wars universe and I really admire that. It doesn't need Han Solo or Luke Skywalker to be a Star Wars game. And the aforementioned moment actually comes as a real reward to an honestly disappointing ending. A pat on the back for working through the difficult sections of RC.

However I have my misgivings with RC. For one it's short. Not any shorter than an average FPS campaign of today, but at the time it was a very short game. There are only a handful of worlds to go to. Although the finales end with a bang (the Republic Ghostship's final mission has the most badass ending setpiece I've ever seen in a Star Wars game), they aren't extremely varied. You're going to be inside military compounds with only a few examples having open level design (these often have squad-points where you can assign snipers and grenadiers). There will be a few stretches where you have to go down a narrow corridor. Fighting waves of enemies. Ho-humming your way along. It'd be an injustice if I didn't emphasis a 'few' though. Most often the game gives you options and some cool set-piece battles to command through.

The game can also be back-breakingly hard at points. I like this, but sometimes you'll get super-bullet spongy enemies (the reason why the main blaster feels shitty) back to back. The super-battle droids are the worst offenders. We're talking fighting up to six of those fuckers at once, in a bare-knuckled shoot-out. On harder difficulties, this can make the game undeniably frustrating. Which turns those glorious finales into a sweat-inducing curse-ridden rant.

Also no sequel. When you finish this game, you will agree that it ends at the worst moment. It doesn't feel unfinished due to just how badass the ending finale is. I mean there's a stretch that basically deconstructs the entire premise of the game and makes you realize just how important your squad is. But story-wise, you'll have to read a book to ever see the end of the Republic Commando series. And honestly, the book was 'meh' like most video game books.

The squad gameplay can be a bit disappointing at times. It's more arcadey than realistic, and sometimes the squadmates are there to just hide how bullet-spongy the enemies are. I'd have liked to be able to always have a guy with his sniper-rifle out rather than them having to setup. I'd also have liked to have the squad mates use grenades more often or engage in melee instead of using those aforementioned blasters. Asking them to switch to shotguns would've been the best damn thing too. 

But every complaint I have with the game ends with a 'however'. The squad gameplay can be meh, however the way the game uses the squad adds extreme weight to the narrative and tone. The story is abrupt, however it has so many moments in the game that have struck with me for a damn decade. The levels aren't varied, however they really give that "behind enemy lines blowing up their shit" feeling.

For $10.00, you get a game that I would mention in the same breath as KotOR 1&2 and Jedi Outcast. It's not just a great Star Wars game, it's a game I would recommend to people that know nothing about the universe. It's a game I would play even if I wasn't in the mood for a Star Wars fix. This was a work of passion for the devs, who used Star Wars as a vehicle to tell a story of cooperation and brotherhood more through the gameplay than cutscenes.

EDIT: Some things I forgot to mentioned or worded poorly. For one the AI of the squadmates is competent, but the enemy droids are as dumb as they are in the Prequels. Only the Super Battle Droid or Droideka pose any threat due to their bullet-spongey nature and their constantly attacking AI pattern. An enemy force you encounter later mixes things up, but their use of cover is only so effective and they do have a habit of mixing effective tactics with standing in the open.

As a whole though, the enemy variety is noteworthy. Each major faction in the Clone Wars (as were present up to episode III) is represented and has units that are both cannon fodder and those that require squad focus fire. The enemy forces are gradually changed out and each world introducing a new faction that is better than the one before. Better armored, armed, and tactical. You'll never meet a force that can truly match your Commandos, but the array or melee and ranged enemies is remarkable for such a short game. 

Also, there is multiplayer in RC. Do I play it? Well, once or twice. It's a deathmatch arena game in the style of older shooters. Make of that what you will.

In this game, you play as Commando Delta 38 (Boss/Leader).
The game follows the story of three missions throughout Delta Squad's career in the Separatist Crisis.
From fighting alongside wookies to getting your face drilled by a scavenger droid, you lead your squad to complete objectives your normal, mass produced, counterparts could/cannot.

The game and story is nice, I loved it and maybe you will too. This is from the soldier's perspective as to the usual jedi perspective. The game plays pretty damn smooth on PC. I haven't had any real game-breaking problems. The game is old enough to even play on lower-end laptops. You get to actually order your squad to do things (ex.When you issue the Search and Destroy order, they become aggressive and move ahead even if you're looking around, You can order them to set demolition charges on objectives to progress or you could order them to secure the area and plant the demolition charge yourself. You can even send them to sniper/anti-armor positions as well as turrets.)

If you lose all your health, you get downed and the game doesn't end until your entire squad is downed. So while you're downed you could either tell them to maintain current orders (ex. search and destroy) or order the closest squad member to revive you. There's also the option to load the last save while you're downed. There's also quicksaves, I hotkeyed mine to F1 and F3 because I can screw things up a lot. 

I don't think you can really get through this game without ordering your squad around. You take quite a bit of damage, even on medium difficulty. Just for future reference, don't run infront of your squad while they're firing a sniper or a anti-armor grenade. Bad things happen. . .

All in all this game was great for it's time and pretty short if you know what you're doing. I just REALLY wish there was a sequal just because of the ending. . .

[h1]TL:DR? See Conclusion[/h1]

[h1]INTRODUCTION:[/h1]
An old game (by the time I wrote this review) but a great game nonetheless.

As you might know, this is a Star Wars game based on the Clone Wars era where you are the leader of an elite Clone Commando Unit tasked with some of the most dangerous and most critical missions in service of the Galactic Republic.

[h1]PROS:[/h1]
+ Story: -Amazing story that places you not in the eyes of a skillful Jedi or a powerful Sith, but in the boots of Clone Troopers fighting the war. The game delivers in terms of story with its superior voice acting by Temuera Morrison (Jango Fett) as well and the various personalities of your squad mates really adds to the experience.

+ Squad Mechanics: -You cannot Rambo (go solo) this game, mainly because the squad is mandatory, BUT also because the game is brutal as hell (like most old FPS games). Enemies are really hard to kill without your squad's support requiring the players to properly order their squads into position and direct their fire when necessary.

+ Graphically pleasing despite its age: -Released on 2005, this game carries a dated visual design, but pleasing nonetheless. Animation is good and the atmosphere is immersive. (I simply love the HUD in this game)

+ Sound: -One of the greatest OST I have ever heard. (Vode An is the greatest of these OST)

+ Gameplay: -Lengthy campaign without getting boring: There is always action around the corner.

[h1]CONS:[/h1]
- Squad AI is a bit limited: -Although the AI, for the most part, is intelligent and is far more useful than some of the other AI partners in modern games, I feel as though a bit more could have been done. They follow command well enough.

- Bugged Graphic setting in terms of Bump Mapping: -Remained unfix to this day. (can be turned off in the options menu though)

[h1]Additional Note:[/h1]
The game is linear (corridor shooting), from start to finish. THIS IS NOT A BAD THING PEOPLE. Not all games need to be open world, specially if the game, such as this one, is trying to properly tell the story in a progressive fashion giving the player a sense of direction and purpose.

[h1]CONCLUSION:[/h1]
MUST BUY and MUST OWN for any Star Wars fan or First Person Shooter fans.

This game is a masterpiece, especially for its time. The gameplay is very dynamic and very fun. The ost is insanely good. The story is charged with emotion while not overexplaining itself, and let you experience it through the gameplay. It also shows a dark and very mature side of the Clone Wars. Here, you are not the main character, a powerful Jedi, or an important clone commander. You are the elite, yes, but unspoken of. You are replaceable, and you fall into the shadows for the greater good with your brothers, "each a part of a whole person", one among millions, and history will probably not remember you.

This is without a doubt the best Star Wars FPS game ever made and arguably one of the best Star Wars games ever made. Dark Forces pales in comparison to this game. The art style, the gameplay, the characters, and the environments are timeless and despite the fact that this game was released over 15 years ago (and has the bad FOV and lack of widescreen to show it) it still holds up. Even despite my immense love and nostalgia for this game, this game is a truly good game whether you like Star Wars or not. If you love good FPS games, reminiscent of Rainbow Six Vegas, you will love this game even if you dont like Star Wars normally.
(Also side note if the dated visual settings on the normal Steam version of this game turn you off from playing it you can download a fix on Moddb called SW Republic Commando fix which allows for 1920x1080 widescreen, modern hd textures and an FOV slider.)

One of the better Star Wars games out there. I despise the prequel trilogy, yet I still found this game to be quite good. It's an FPS where you play as the leader of an elite squad of commandos sent on the toughest of jobs.

You can position your squad members, each one is supposedly skilled at different tasks, and it's mostly just blasting your way through droids and bugs in caverns, facilities, and space ships. You get the typical weapons--shotguns, pistols, sniper, rifle, etc. mostly in star-wars-style laser blasting form. 

It's about ten hours long, and it's a pretty good campaign with some neat set-pieces. The squad members have some fun personalities and the voice work is solid. Since it's an older game, there are no iron sights, so that might be hard to get used to. The graphics hold up well, although I do believe it lacks widescreen. There are some compatibility issues, so you might need to take a look at the forums if you run into problems.

Summary first:

It's a nice shooter, fairly straight forward. Perfect if you're looking for a small diversion involving firefights and lasers. (Note: I didn't try multiplayer. The option exists, that's all I can say about it) I'd still recommend waiting for a sale.


And now a bit more detail about the gameplay:

It really is quite simple. You have a standard selection of Star Warsy rifles (automatic, explosive, sniper) and pistols, plus a swappable slot where you can pick up whatever special weapon enemies are currently dropping, including some heavy weapons. There's also a nifty melee attack, plus visor spatter when you get too close. (Doesn't qualify as gore exactly, if you worry about those things, but the helmet / HUD design was overall a very nice touch)
The squad mechanics are kept very simple as well. You have three teammates, who, despite some reviews, are reasonably smart and effective. They soak and deal damage for you, rarely get in the way and generally make themselves useful. The squad is controlled by setting a general stance (aggressive, defensive, staying close) or by assigning individuals to special positions that are part of the map: gun turrets and sniping/heavy weapons/grenade spots. You can also designate a priority target.
Best of all: When someone (including you) is downed, they can be revived. And there are no objectives that depend on your squaddies: no failing a mission because some thick-headed yet mission-critical muppet got themselves killed. (Looking at you, Opposing Force welder!) In fact, if need be you can even perform tasks usually left to AI characters yourself.



The difficulty isn't a huge issue. The game is quite manageable even on hard difficulty, thanks to the squad and the option to have them revive even you. (On demand, no less) The game can get quite tough for those stretches where you work alone, though. Having some folks around to revive you after you've blown yourself up with a grenade thinking you're pressing the zoom button really helps. Not that I'd ever do that. You'll also miss not being shot at quite so much.

The level design is a bit barren, to be honest, but the maps are fairly large and overall the graphics are okay. (Hard to think back over ten years now). The three main settings / themes are Geonosis, a Star Destroyer (or whatever they're called before the Imperial Navy got hold of them) and Kashyyyk (jungle, no guarantee on the number of ys). Mercifully the game doesn't have you plod through every movie scene but follows its own narrative that loosely connects to events from the movies and (possibly) elsewhere. 

Always worth mentioning for SW-games is the music: Unlike virtually every other Star Wars game over the past twenty years, this game (almost) avoids blindly recycling the well-known music themes from the movies. If you like Star Wars games you've probably heard it [i]everywhere[/i], an infernal loop literally orchestrated by John Williams. But this game is not quite as blatant about it. The music does, for once, actually fit the setting, and I don't recognise all the tunes from the movies (and all the other games, bloody hell). So under the circumstances that probably qualifies as being creative and original. Well done, I suppose. Another bonus point: Doesn't use the Dagobah theme even in the jungle setting. Given this franchise's track record that's just amazing.

I remember playing this game way back on the original Xbox. It's not through rose-colored glasses that I say this is the greatest squad-based shooter I've ever played.

Let's start with the atmosphere. It's spot on. Any casual Star Wars fan will recognize most of the enemies and locations. The level and character designs are grittier than what you see in the movies, and that fits the tone perfectly. The HUD is one of the best I've ever seen, because YOU SEE THE BORDERS OF YOUR HELMET! Such a simple design choice affects your immersion immensely.

So everything around you is cool. What about the combat? This game FEELS great. The modular weapons system is genius.  The squad commands are easy to learn but hard to master. The difficulty is pleasantly challenging; don't expect yourself to be repeating tons of levels, but do expect to be constantly searching for health and ammo. The weapons feel rewarding to use, and above all, the squad-based combat is amazing. You FEEL bad-ass. You FEEL like it's you four protagonists against the world. And you WANT to take 'em all on.

Your three Clone Commando compatriots, Scorch, Fixer, and Sev, are exceptional AI companions (especially for 2005). They are effective in combat, respond to commands instantly, and generally don't make the kind of dumb decisions that make you rage at AI companions. They don't talk much, but you can still feel personality emanating from them.

On the note of character, the one category where this game falters is story. You know where you are, and you know why. You have objectives. But that's about it. The characters don't change over time. There are no plot twists. There is an instance of tragic loss (I won't spoil it for you), and it hits you hard. But there is room for improvement in that area.

Besides the story, what other improvements could be made? I won't comment on the graphics, because this game is coming up on 10 years old, but I will say they've aged well. The only thing that springs to mind is the level design. Don't get me wrong, the levels are designed fine, but it gives away what's to come. When you see a spot where you can issue a sniping command, you know there's enemies directly ahead. Health and ammo are always located directly behind large groups of enemies. It's textbook old-fashioned level design, but you always know what's coming.

One final point: because this is an older game, a 1920x1080 aspect ratio is not an option it offers. It's a minor detail, but an important one.

In conclusion, ten years later, this is still an incredible game. Although the story is never going to be a selling point, everything else about this game is great. It feels like you're taking a first-person trip through the summer action film spectacular that Star Wars never had. I highly recommend it to anyone who puts gameplay ahead of graphics. Amongst the vast troves of LucasArts treasures, this gem certainly shines bright.

A truly singular Star Wars FPS gaming experience even to this day, Republic Commando puts you in command as a "squad" (really it's a fireteam) of four elite commandos tasked with doing-things-Republic-Commandos-would-do. The game follows a formula the likes of which you just don't see these days anymore. That being, a semi-tactical, or arcade-tactical experience where placement and management of your commandos and co-operation within the squad is key to getting through the stages in one piece.

Novel today, and still somewhat novel in its time, the game includes some basic commands for your squad, (Hold/Follow/Assault/Break off), and other actions which are entirely contextual, (highlight a context and the ghost-image of your squad member will appear on it per the action). On the map you'll often find positions where you are able to set up a squad-mate to use a powerful weapon in a stationary mode, sacrificing mobility for high-damage covering fire. This is often just before and during big set-piece fights, and this is where the break-off command comes in handy, as that commando will remain in that spot until manually detached via context command, using the break-off (all) command, or if you move too far away.

Character design is highly stylized, with everything from B1 battle droids, B2s, wookiees, and even Geonosians tending to feature larger, more intimidating and grittier aesthetics. It is not 1:1 with Star Wars canon by and large, but the sheer charisma of these commandos has retroactively worked its way back into canon (minus their personal shields). Here is where the notion began though, and we're grateful for it.

Your squad is decently competent, and while the standard rapid-firing blaster rifle you all share has a high fire rate and very little recoil, its damage against any heavier types of enemies is relatively low. This is where coordinated fire and sharing enemy aggro comes into play. Each commando is equipped with recharging personal shielding, (the likes of which were popularized by Halo/Mass Effect), and for the most part, outside of boss type enemies, most AI including your commados shoot in bursts, which means in ideal circumstances, any commando that is hit while exposed, can return to cover while another exposes himself to shoot, and can keep their shields up that way.

That is ideal circumstances, and more often than not a single commando will tend to remain exposed for longer, whittling their shields down until they are wounded or knocked into a downed state. Against fodder this is rare, but against heavies, unless aggro is very evenly spread, this is likely.

This is where it gets interesting. You can order a commando to, or you yourself can, revive a downed commando, but this takes another commando out of the fight for several seconds to get done. There are many instances where every bit of firepower is needed to cull a threat before reviving can get done, and this can even happen to you. In a downed state you can order your men to maintain orders, (and thus keep fighting), call one of them to break off and revive you, or you can load from a save state. (The game also features quicksave/quickload). When fighting is over they will automatically move to revive any downed teammate.

While the revives are free, you will not revive with full health. The game is littered with a smattering of bacta stations to account for this, as having a whole team at low health can be dangerous when facing heavy opposition. The shields only account for so much damage mitigation, and enemy melee attacks get through all shielding, so cover and "sharing the hate" are always smart moves. One final feature the game includes is using the interact button to highlight a particular enemy to pick out, after which all of your commandos will attempt to take them down. This highlight outlines the enemy through walls/cover, and also displays their health bar until they are killed. I don't use this quite as often as I'd rather my commandos seek out their own targets, but it's handy for bosses or minimal-opposition encounters to track highly mobile enemies or focus fire.

All in all, the gameplay holds up very well in 2026, and with multiple grenade types, strong melee attacks and personal shielding it's fairly akin to halo, with a mix of ADS/down-the-sight aiming for most weapons included. The sound design is handled very well, the acting is superb, and the soundtrack is incredibly evocative. If you're a fan of Star Wars and/or military stuff, or military Star Wars stuff, you shouldn't miss this.

This game absolutely deserves a remaster, and this whole genre of tactical, squad-based FPS game is fairly absent in today's market. Co-operative, or even competitive games, where players each command a squad would be fascinating, and it basically untapped today.

Star Wars: Republic Commando is a squad based shooter set during the Clone Wars. You and a crack squad of Clone commandos navigate a number of high risk operations in a bid to turn back the endless tide from the Confederacy forces. But is the game enjoyable to play? This is what I think of Republic Commando.

Republic Commando is a fantastic game even today. It's such a shame that it never got a sequel, or that no one has made another Star Wars game with the same concepts. Battlefront lets you play as a normal soldier on the ground but this game goes one better by giving you a squad of unique elite clone troopers and running you through a fantastic, if far too short, campaign from Geonosis right through to the invasion of Kashyyyk. The graphics haven't aged too badly in my opinion and some of the level design is exquisite. You can expect the usual excellent Star Wars tracks playing during the game, as well as some unique to the game. It is all suitably epic. I thoroughly enjoyed my time with it.

The story starts with you growing up as a clone, along with your squad, and showing the squad develop into the efficient killing machines they are in the game with some starting cutscenes. You are then thrown into the maelstrom of the Clone Wars as the Republic begin the war in earnest on Geonosis. You are Delta 38, Boss, voiced excellently by the definitive clone trooper voice Temuera Morrison. You lead the rest of Delta Squad, 40, 62 and 07 known as Fixer, Scorch and Sev respectively. Each trooper has his own personality and the banter between them is excellent. Together, you fight through hell and back and you can really get behind this band of brothers.

Republic Commando doesn't do anything radically different to shake up the genre but commanding your squad and using the rudimentary tactics feels great. You have an assortment of weaponry to use in your battles, as well as being able to set your squad up in sniping positions or grenade points whilst you flank the enemy and performing breach and clear maneuvers. The level design is excellent, with a number of well done set pieces complimenting the strong gameplay. There is a good variety of enemies as well, each with different strengths and weaknesses. I always found it odd that it was so easy to take down Super Battle Droids in Battlefront but here they really earn the "Super" title as they are heavily armoured walking shields that shoot at you. A negative is the short campaign, clocking in at just under 8 hours. That itself isn't a problem, but the game has three acts each set in a location. Geonosis, on board an abandoned Republic ship and Kashyyyk. With the entire Clone Wars conflict, they could have included more locations whilst still keeping it fresh. A missed opportunity there. 

Another complaint can be made about the AI. Too often it feels like you have to carry the rest of your clone brothers and it's hit and miss whether they'll be effective or not, especially during some of the set pieces. They can often wander out into the open and get gunned down, won't do as they're told and other silly little things you probably have come to expect from AI in a video game. It's all par for the course.  This isn't a negative, but the cameo is strong with Star Wars games. If it doesn't have a character from the films, is it even a Star Wars game? All jokes aside, they are done well and integrated nicely in the story.

Overall, I think Republic Commando is one of the best Star Wars games period, right up there with Kotor, Battlefront and the Jedi Knight series. It makes me a little sad we probably won't see the likes of these games again but we are lucky to have them available here on Steam. With its great level design, enjoyable campaign and decent FPS gameplay, this is one Star Wars game you need to play. You won't regret it.

Wow, where to begin. First of all, this is without question not only my favorite First Person Shooter of all time, but my favorite video game of all time. In fact, Republic Commando is the game that got me into PC gaming in the first place. I still remember years ago when it came out, seeing one of my friends playing it on his gaming rig, and being absolutely blown away by the concept, sound, graphics, and atmosphere. Now of course, this was back in 2005, so it may not blow people away any more with its graphics, but it is still an incredibly satisfying shooter experience. My steam hours in this game pale I'm sure to the many hours I poured into this game before I had steam and when I had the game on disc. 

First of all, with Republic Commando it's the details that matter - and this game gets the details right, every time. You play as the leader of an elite spec ops squad consisting of four clone commandos called "Delta Squad" during the Clone Wars, and each Commando has his own distinct personality and traits. They even got the guy who played Jango Fett in Attack of the Clones to voice your character, a nice touch indeed. To this day, years later, I have been unable to find a game that has a more intuitive, responsive squad command system. It's simple, but effective, mostly because your squadmates are not the helpess AI that most games tend to have, but they can actually get the job done, regardless of if you're there or not. Take a round to the face and fall to the ground? No problem, the commandos of Delta Squad will carry on the fight, often engaging in hand to hand combat with the enemy (which is incredibly fun to watch) before they come back to revive you.

I won't go into all the nitty gritty details of gameplay. Suffice it to say, any fan of first person shooters and squad based games will be immensely satisfied. What I will focus on for the remainder of my review is the fact that this game gets every detail right, time after time.

First off, your squadmates. Holy hell, Lucasarts hit the ball out of the park with this one. Each commando has his own personality, and the dialogue between the four of them, including the commando you play as, nicknamed "Boss", is very entertaining.  They'll banter back and forth, often joking with each other and comparing dead enemies to each other's mothers (I mean, they [i] are [/i] clones who don't have mothers, but still, it's funny). The game also has a cool feature where if you die, you stay there on the ground, waiting for your squadmates to revive you, and you can either order them to maintain their current orders or come rescue you, a nice touch for sure that makes you avoid the usual frustration with AI in games. You can also revive your squadmates if they go down, and the only time you have to go back to a save is when every commando has gone down - if one clone is still standing, the fight goes on. 

And then, of course, there's the sound and the atmosphere - from the moment the game starts on Kamino to the brutal ending firefights on Kashyyyk, the sound design in the game is simply flawless. It's over ten years later, and this game is [i] still [/i] a joy to crank up and enjoy with surround sound. The game takes place over the course of three large missions - one that takes place on Geonosis (and later in a Confederacy droid factory) at the beginning of the Clone Wars, one that takes place on an abandoned Republic ghost ship in space (my personal favorite), and one that takes place on Kashyyyk at the very end of the Clone Wars (tying in nicely with Revenge of the Sith, which came out right at the same time). Each environment is very well-designed, even by modern standards. 

Beyond the commandos and the atmosphere, there's something else going on here too, something a little deeper. This is a [i] war [/i] game. And Lucasarts got every detail right. There are no Jedi in this game. There is no "save the day" moment where the fate of the galaxy rests in your hands. You're simply another grunt, albeit a well trained one, in the long and brutal conflict of the Clone Wars. This is not just a Star Wars game - this is a war game. The Commandos get tired, they complain about the waves of enemies they face, they even seem to suffer from mental exhaustion sometimes, firing extra rounds into already dead enemies as if the stresses of war have become too much, even for a special forces clone. I'm still shocked that such a gritty attention to military detail was put into a Star Wars game, as you actually see the clones experiencing combat fatigue as the war goes on. Now, this isn't some super-deep Apocalypse Now or Heart of Darkness story, but it's still compelling nonetheless. Heck, the game even ends with a rock song, a sharp departure from the style of other Star Wars games, but a very fitting one nonetheless. 

I'll quickly touch on the enemies you face, too. You fight waves of Trandoshan slavers, mercenaries, battle droids, super battle droids, droidekas, and other even larger enemies. And, on harder difficulty settings, it can be a challenge. Super battle droids can annihilate your entire squad in a matter of seconds, and that chubby Trandoshan with the shotgun running at you? Yeah, he can pump one blast right into your face and you're a dead man. Super Battle Droids in particular are nasty enemies in this game - they have much deeper voices than the movies, and fire what basically amounts to a rapid fire cannon out of their arm that can flatten you in two or three hits. Overall, the diverse enemies in Republic Commando contribute a great deal to the gritty feel of the game. 

I could go on and on - about how awesome the weapon choices are, how immersive the ambient sound in the game is, how jarring and frightening some of the enemies you face are, but I'll leave that to you to discover when you buy and play this game, which I very much hope you do. To recap, if you like:

-Squad Based Shooters
-Any type of Shooter, for that matter
-Star Wars
-Shooters that get that gritty war feeling [i] right [/i]
-Immersive, intense single-player campaigns
-Sci Fi in general
-Sci Fi shooters
(You get the idea...)

Star Wars: Republic Commando is a first person tactical shooter set in a science fiction universe, I don't know which one. Set during the clone wars, you and your squad get to go to planets featured in the prequel trilogy so you can shoot droids and other things who had the audacity to not be born human. 
You start the game with a DC-15s side arm blaster, as well as the DC-17m interchangeable weapon system, which is an assault rifle of sorts that can have its parts changed out with sniper rifle and grenade launcher attachments.

Its a neat system, where a majority of your weapons are technically just the two, but you do pick up some other weapons along the way, usually something you pulled out of the cold dead grip of something you killed. The spread gun is my favorite. 

The guns feel nice to use, with good sound effects and crunchy outcomes on whatever you're wasting. Droids fall apart, and the more squishy targets tend to explode into a burst of blood before toppling over like a rag doll. You also have a melee attack, with the most common being just deploying a blade on your fist and punching a fool with it. 

Other than usual mooks like B1 battle droids, bugs, and lizard BASTARDS, you also have larger, beefier enemies like the B2 Super battle droid and whatever the flying Geonosian with the beam gun is. Throughout the game you'll also come across Spider Droids, who only exist to soak up your ammo and make you upset. 

As long as someone in your squad is alive, you're still in the fight, which is a nice anti-frustration device. You can be revived from a down state as long as a squad member is alive as well as they can be revived by you or another squad member.

The game is a console port, so the squad tactics isn't really Rainbow six levels of detailed. You can tell them where to go, give them basic follow or kill orders, and have them stack on doors for breach and clear movements. You can also order them to do objectives for you like slicing into a system or setting up a bomb to destroy a target. They're competent enough, so you don't end up doing everything yourself. 

Much like my day to day life, Republic Commando is also surprisingly violent. With the aforementioned blood, the game tends to get a little messy from time to time. Blood can splatter on to your visor, there are some scenes with the good crimson stuff splattered on the walls, and you can find some Clone Troopers with their limbs and even noggin' removed. 
Geonosians can also just flat out explode into bits after being shot or stabbed, limbs hilariously rolling away because the physics glitched out. 

The game is fun, everything about the game is competent which really helps to elevate Republic Commando as more than just another Star Wars game.
Everything except the last few missions of the game.

The game isn't really that long, about six or seven hours or so. But even then it really starts to drag on near the end. Once you reach the final part of the game you're assaulted with samey hall ways and a rapid fire barrage of the same objectives over and over again. 

You're also overwhelmed with dozens of the toughest enemies in the game which soak up even more ammo and become a complete drag to fight since its just one encounter with 4 or 5 super battle droids after another. Mix this together with CIS drop pods that constantly spawn new droids that get dropped into areas in the scientific numbers known as a shit ton. 
Then you have to take out these drop pods with explosives that can take anywhere from 10 to 20 seconds to plant. Now mix these together with slicing or other objectives that can take 2 or so minutes to finish, and you're stuck just waiting in between annoying fire fights with annoying enemies. 

Its the worst aspects of the game all crammed into one area of the game. And then it has the balls to break your heart at the end. 

Other than that, game's fine. Its darker take on Star Wars, orchestral score, crunchy shooting, and cool premise do a lot to carry the game past it's shortcomings. 

Other interesting things, I guess.

Republic Commando came out months before Revenge of the Sith, and I guess the developers didn't really get the memo from Lucas Films when they were developing Republic Commandos. Because of this, there is a lot of things absent that's actually kind of interesting when you compare RC to Revenge. 
Here's some examples. 

The clone troopers never switch from phase I to phase II power armor, even well over a year into the war. The Venator Star Destroyer is missing entirely, making every Republic ship just the Acclamator baby boy Star Destroyer. 
The ARC-170 is nowhere to be seen either, with the V-19 Torrent filling in for it well after the ARC-170 was introduced during the Clone Wars. 

Its not the game's fault, I'm not criticizing it like some kind of nerd. I'm just saying its kind of interesting to see. 

Republic Commando is pretty great, save for the last hour or two of the game. I'd recommend it, get it on sale, or fist fight someone for it, I don't know.

This game is a tactical first person shooter taking place in the Star Wars universe. You play as a team of four different commandos fighting for the Galactic Republic in the Clone Wars as they battle the Confederacy on a variety of different landscapes and with different weapons. Each team member has different abilities that can be used in different circumstances.

Like I said, this game is fine, it's aged just fine, it plays just fine, and it's a great bargain. It's fine. Just fine.

It is a tactical shooter, which means that you can command your teammates to do a number of different tasks, take cover and attack in a specific defensive formation, and help revive each other after being shot down. This works best when you are in a large open room with ample debris to take cover behind while waves and waves of enemies attack, which happens all too often. It feels satisfying to peg down the most efficient formation between you and your team where you can effectively mow down oncoming enemies without being wiped out yourselves. It's also pretty nifty to tactically advance down a corridor, sending your boys to cover, leap frogging them, and then covering them while they advance. However, for the most part this is unnecessary since you can usually just book it down the hallway without any consequences so long as you stop before triggering any alarms, rendering that mechanic useless. 

The game also has some forced decisions sections like where you can choose to either breach the door with explosives and gun down every surprised enemy a la Call of Duty, or quietly hack your way through the door and stealthily kill them. The thing is, it doesn't really matter which you choose. The stealth route is longer but much easier and the explosive route deals more damage to your team but is less boring. Both are equally viable in every circumstance. I think the best way to have done that is give you the options and switch up which is best for each scenario and force you to gather limited intel and make a decision that actually matters.

The shooting feels fine. Just fine. The space guns have a good weight and accuracy and are fun enough to shoot and there is a variety of other weapons available, such as rocket launchers, miniguns, sniper rifles, and actual lead shooting guns which are kinda fun to shoot. There are also different turrets that fire different projectiles that are effective in different circumstances. So, for instance you could command your guys to man the anti tank gun while you take on the little guys. 

There is quite a variety of enemy types, including robots, pig people, bug people, tanks, and mechs. It gets pretty chaotic in a larger room with a wide array of different enemy types and that's when the game is at its best because it's taking advantage of your teams abilities and your strategic skills. However, a lot of this game is walking down down a corridor, sometimes alone without your crew, taking down a smattering of boring enemies or bullet spongy mini bosses and moving to the next checkpoint. There are even designated stealth sections, but they don't automatically insta fail you for triggering the alarms they just through the entire enemy army at you.

The best part of this game is definitely the character development. The story is super ho hum, each mission has a different setting and a different objective completely independent from the last one or the next one, and the last mission is Star Wars Saving Private Ryan. The thing that matters most about war stories isn't the action, but the characters, and each individual character in this game is very well developed and portrayed. They banter back in forth during and between missions and organically build a relationship between each other. 

In essence, a decent game with decent shooting and good character writing. Would recommend to Star Wars fans.

this game is just amazing

its like rainbow six vegas 2 only with more in depth story telling and character development

republic commando's tells a tail of delta squad, an elite clone trooper squad consisting of four members (plus command but im not counting him) each with their own personalitys and voices (voices which i find kinda odd considering the lore of the game being they are all clones of the same person but honestly whatever it adds to the plot so who cares) of which kinda give off a sort of teenage mutant ninja turtles vibe but in a lot more dark and gritty setting

Sev aka 07 the sniper, the white and red edgy yet not to stereotypical type edgy clone that seems the most badass but also has a few quirks visable throughout the campaign. (like forgetting to push an elevator button). he's basically the raphiel of the group.

Scorch aka 62 the demolitions expert. basically the comic relief character thats kinda like michalangelo or however you spell his name. wearing the white, black, and orange armor he seems the most.... unqalified member of the group at first but does his job, and does it well.

Fixer (yeah thats his nickname. kinda lazy but whatever) aka 40 the tech expert is the don of the group. being the one good at computers and wearing the green and white armor. honestly id kinda say hes the least interesting of the group aside from boss which i will get to after but he's still a thing.

and finally the protagonist which you play as: Boss (also lackluster name but whatever) aka 38. his roll being well... take a guess. he wears orange and white armor. nothing much to him aside from him being kinda the most bland and jango fett esc of the bunch but at least he cares for his team.

all are tasked with doing the republics seemingly most difficult missions all on their own none the less.

something worth mentioning about this game which i personally liked the most being: Republic commando does something a lot of star wars media and games alike doesnt really do all that much of.

It shows the darker more in depth scary side of war. In this game you arent a lightsaber weilding jedi trying to figure out if what he is doing is right or not, you arent a major componint of the story like anakin skywalker or obi-wan.

you're just a clone. a soldier. one in a million, doing a job.

you get to see first hand the horrors of whats really happening out there.

you get to see what it does to people.

you hear the screams, see the death, and none of it is glorified movie haha he fell funny type death. it makes you feel uneasy. sure there are some comical moments when taking out enemy troops, but even then they managed to nail something a lot if not every game fails to do. make you feel a bit bad for the things you do. even the droids screaming upon death sends a chill down your spine briefly. but eventually, like a soldier, you just tune it out. try to ignore it. and do your job.

another thing being the characters. you actually feel for your squad mates. unlike most games where your team is just paper thin and not much depth to them, you get attatched. you can not only hear how your team feels for eachother during battlefield banter, but also see it in just simple actions during cutscenes or in game actions. which makes the ending feel all that much more heartbreaking when you know there isnt going to be a sequal anytime soon. at least not one that has the same power put into it as the original lucas films had. lord knows disney wont bother.

you can tell the game has passion put into it. it has more advanced multiplayer customization then halo did at the time they both released, the character models each have their own style and work put in. its not just clean spotless armor you can see on your team the battle damage and scratches from conflicts past.

plus one of the most prominant fetures that they DIDNT EVEN HAVE TO DO IN THE FIRST PLACE is the iconic helmet.

the helmet visor doesnt take up to much of your screen. it looks great, and it feels great. like a real high tech helmet. they coulda just had it be a simple screen with a minor hud. but oh no they made you feel like a clone and it felt great. not to mention the most iconic thing about the helmet: the cleaning feature.

few games let blood and water and whatnot get on the players camara.

little to no games that ive seen make it so it doesnt just fade away. theres actually something that cleans it off.

thats the ammount of pure detail this game has put into it. the ammount of pure love and compassion it has.

it makes me sad yet happy at the same time

sad that it will probably never get a sequal.

but happy that its legacy will never be slandered, ruined and perverted by todays gaming company's values of money over quality.

while RC is not necessarily one the best games ever or anything like that it is definitely a good game and most definitely one of the most interesting and fun star wars games. 

Why is it interesting? because you're not a Jedi or a chosen one or a general, your an elite grunt, a clone commando nothing more, nothing less. You see the clone wars through the eyes of a soldier, you never even directly see a Jedi or high up Republic officer, the closest you get is helping Tarful, spotting General Grievous for a few seconds, hearing a Republic Navy captain, and seeing a fleet wide transmission by Yoda. While there are grand moments of heroism their still acts of regular (if exceptionally skilled and equipped) people not the superpowered acrobatics of Jedi or the grand decisions of Generals but the tenacity and bravery of individual "small" people. The whole game almost has more in common with Band of Brothers or a movie about Delta force than star wars, sometimes you get there in time to rescue people sometimes not, other times you just help where you can before moving on with you actual objectives. Also shout to the voice actors for giving the troopers distinct and memorable characters.

The game play is a blast, since there's no force powers you need to use the good blaster at your side, along with whatever dead enemies drop, to complete your objectives, good aim and methodical movement are key and it's extremely rewarding when you manage to pick apart enemy forces before they even manage to get a hit, or survive an ambush at point blank with a decent amount of health. Your squadmates are also pretty damned competent and can be trusted to do as told 85% of the time. The enemy AI is nothing to write home about though, it's not bad but it's also not great.

On the technical side the game has aged but honestly it hasn't done so particularly poorly nor particularly well, it looks fine, it runs on modern systems pretty well, though in my experience you should leave bump mapping to low or it crashes when you try to load a level. The UI is ok at max resolution but it is a tiny bit distorted, the sound effects are all really well done. the downside is that it's not a very long game, probably around 8-12 hours on hard when you know what you're doing.

TLDR; Thoroughly recommended, a short but grounded and well realised star wars story in the vein of a war movie. 9/10
